memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up, and there were the Egyptians,
marching after them. They were terrified and cried out to the LORD."
- Ex 14:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They looked up, and there was the army.

The Bible does not hide their reaction. They were terrified. These were not
spiritual heroes with unshakeable calm. They were ordinary, frightened people
watching the most powerful army in the world come over the horizon.

But look at what fear did: "they cried out to the LORD." Before the complaining
begins in the next verse, the first instinct was prayer.

That is worth noticing, because we tend to think fear is a spiritual failure. It
is not. Fear is a human response. What matters is the direction it moves us.
Fear can drive us away from God into panic and blame, or it can drive us toward
Him.

David wrote, "When I am afraid, I put my trust in you" (Ps 56:3). Notice he does
not say "I am never afraid." He says when.

If you are frightened today, you have not failed. The question is simply where
the fear takes you. Cry out. Scripture is full of people who did exactly that,
and God did not scold them for it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where does fear usually take you first, to God or to worry?
2. What are you afraid of right now that you have not actually prayed about?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I am afraid, and I bring that fear straight to You rather than carrying it
alone. Help me to trust You in it. Amen.
